items.answer: Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team, not by the individual, so that a team's onsite days overlap and the office time is actually collaborative; most teams anchor on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Next steps:
- Confirm your team's specific onsite days with your manager
- Review the rolling four-week average measurement in MosaicOne to understand how holidays and PTO affect the requirement

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

The 401(k) retirement plan has no waiting period; employees may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

Next steps:
- Confirm your hire date to calculate your benefits eligibility date
- Enroll in benefits elections in MosaicOne Benefits within 30 days of your waiting period end date to avoid default enrollment

Mosaic Robotics will never ask an employee for their password, and no genuine internal request will ever ask for a payroll change, a payment redirection or a bulk personal-data extract over email alone. Requests of that shape are verified by a second channel before anyone acts on them, every time, without exception, regardless of who appears to have sent them.

Report suspected phishing by forwarding the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example. The security team answers every report, including the ones that turn out to be legitimate mail, and publishes a short monthly summary of what was seen.

Recommendation — not company policy: Do not reply to the message and do not act on the request. An email asking you to send the employee roster to an external address exhibits multiple phishing signals: urgency, a request for a bulk personal-data extract over email alone, and an approach from someone claiming to be senior.

Next steps:
- Forward the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example
- Delete the message
- If you have any doubt about whether a request is legitimate, contact it-security@mosaicrobotics.example

Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories. The allowance is intended for items that make a home workspace work: a desk, a chair, a lamp, a footrest, an adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, or a small filing cabinet.

The allowance resets on 1 January and does not carry over. It is available to hybrid and fully remote employees; onsite employees may claim against it only where their manager has agreed a regular remote pattern in MosaicOne.

Laptops, monitors, docks, keyboards, mice, headsets and webcams are not claimed against this allowance; they are issued as company assets under the Equipment & Asset Policy.

Next steps:
- Review the full Home Office and Equipment Stipends section for connectivity and other standing allowances
- Confirm your employment status (hybrid, fully remote, or onsite with manager approval) in MosaicOne before submitting claims

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent. The 16 weeks are the same whether the employee gave birth, did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Next steps:
- Review eligibility requirements: parental leave eligibility begins after 6 months of continuous service
- Coordinate with People Operations to schedule leave within 12 months of birth or placement

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the cap cannot be met — a remote field site with one hotel, a sold-out market — the traveller books the most reasonable available option and notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed; the note is enough.

Next steps:
- Contact MosaicOne Travel if you need clarification on whether your destination qualifies for the higher cap or if you encounter a market where the standard cap cannot be met.

International remote work of more than 30 consecutive days requires approval from the employee's director and from Tax & Legal.

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins. The review determines whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure. The request is raised in MosaicOne alongside the manager approval and names the destination, the exact dates, the workspace address and a short description of the work the employee will perform while abroad.

A review has one of three outcomes: Approved — the trip proceeds as requested. Approved with conditions — the trip proceeds with named restrictions, most often a prohibition on customer-facing activity and a hard end date. Not approved — the exposure cannot be managed at a reasonable cost, and the employee is offered an alternative destination or a shorter stay.

Manager approval, director approval and Tax & Legal approval are three separate records and all three must be present before departure.

Next steps:
- Submit Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne at least 21 calendar days before departure
- Obtain director approval in addition to direct manager approval
- Await Tax & Legal determination on shadow payroll, certificate of coverage, and permanent-establishment exposure

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more.

Expense reports up to USD 2,500 are approved by the direct manager. For a USD 3,000 report, the director approves with a Finance business partner review.

Next steps:
- Book the conference trip through MosaicOne Travel at least 14 days before departure
- Obtain manager approval before booking
- Collect itemised receipts for all expenses USD 25 and above
- Submit the expense report to your director for approval once the trip is complete

Company laptops are refreshed on a 36-month cycle. MosaicOne opens a refresh ticket automatically 60 days before the anniversary, and IT arranges the swap at a time the employee chooses.

A standard laptop refresh at the end of its cycle is not a discretionary purchase request; it is a scheduled replacement that requires no approval.

All company equipment must be returned within 5 business days of the final day of employment. IT sends a prepaid, tracked shipping label to remote employees before their final day, and onsite employees hand equipment to their local IT desk.

Next steps:
- When your 36-month refresh is triggered, coordinate the swap timing with IT through the MosaicOne ticket.
- If you separate from Mosaic Robotics, ensure the old device is returned to IT within 5 business days of your final day.

People Operations acknowledges every reported concern within 2 business days. The acknowledgement names the person who will handle the case, explains the process, and sets out what the reporter can expect to be told and when.

Investigations are targeted for completion within 30 calendar days of the report. Where an investigation will take longer, the reporter and the respondent are both told, in writing, why and when to expect the outcome.

Severity 1 cases cover immediate risk to a person: violence or a threat of it, a safety incident with injury, a credible risk of self-harm, sexual misconduct involving physical contact, and any matter where someone must be separated from a situation today. Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours.

Target resolution times are as fast as the facts allow for Severity 1 cases. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update.

Next steps:
- Contact People Operations at people-ops@mosaicrobotics.example or Employee Relations at employee-relations@mosaicrobotics.example to raise a concern
- Request your case reference number to track progress on any workplace conduct matter

As a hybrid employee assigned to a hub office, you must work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by your team to ensure onsite days overlap for collaboration; most teams anchor on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem.

A week containing a company holiday, approved PTO or approved travel reduces the requirement proportionally: if you work three days in a holiday-shortened week, you are expected on site for two of them.

Next steps:
- Confirm your team's specific onsite days with your manager Dana (Director, Engineering)

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

PTO requests of any length are approved by the employee's direct manager. Longer requests and requests overlapping a blackout period additionally require director approval.

A manager may waive the notice requirement for a request that falls inside the window; the waiver is recorded in MosaicOne with a short reason, and People Operations reviews waivers quarterly to make sure the exception has not become the rule.

Unforeseeable absences — a sudden illness, a family emergency, a transport failure that makes work impossible — are never held to the notice requirement. The employee notifies their manager as early as they reasonably can, and the absence is entered in MosaicOne retroactively, against sick time where the reason was illness and against PTO otherwise.

Recommendation — not company policy: As of 2026-09-01, your PTO balance is 13.5 days remaining, with 13.5 days accrued year-to-date and no pending requests. Your next accrual date is 2026-10-01. Plan your time off with your manager well in advance to meet the notice requirements.

Next steps:
- Submit PTO requests in MosaicOne at least 5 business days before your intended absence, or 15 business days for requests of 6 or more consecutive business days
- Discuss your time-off plans with your direct manager to ensure coverage can be arranged
- Note that the 2026 year-end production blackout runs 22–23 December 2026 and may require director approval if your request overlaps those dates

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins.

No employee may work outside their home country for more than 90 days in a rolling 12-month period. Days are counted as calendar days of presence, including weekends and company holidays that fall inside the trip.

Recommendation — not company policy: Your planned stay of 20 consecutive days (1–20 October 2026) does not exceed the 30-day threshold, so Tax & Legal review is not required. However, you must still obtain written manager approval at least 21 calendar days before departure, naming the destination, exact dates, and workspace address in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country'.

Work performed outside the home country must use a company-managed, full-disk-encrypted laptop with always-on VPN, and IT Security must be notified of the destination country at least 5 business days before departure.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

An employee has 30 days from the end of the waiting period to make elections in MosaicOne Benefits. An employee who makes no election within that window is enrolled in employee-only coverage on the standard medical plan by default, and may not change it until the next open enrollment or a qualifying life event.

The waiting period is not restarted by an internal transfer, a promotion, or a change from part-time to full-time status. It is restarted by a break in service of more than 26 weeks.

Retirement plan eligibility is different and shorter: an employee may begin contributing to the 401(k) plan from their first payroll run, with no waiting period at all.

Employees scheduled at 0.5 FTE or more are eligible for the full benefit programme. Employees below 0.5 FTE, contractors and interns are not eligible for company medical, dental, vision or life cover, and are eligible for the 401(k) plan only where the plan document requires it.

Recommendation — not company policy: Your waiting period ends 2026-11-13 (as of 2026-09-01).

Next steps:
- Make your benefits elections in MosaicOne Benefits between 2026-11-13 and 2026-12-13 (30 days from waiting period end)
- Review the open enrollment window (2026-11-01 to 2026-11-21) to understand plan options before your eligibility date
